title: Secure autotune change commit and forensic logging
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add end-to-end security and compliance controls for automated batching/caching recommendations and automatic config apply/rollback. Scope: design RBAC for autotune commits, implement cryptographically verifiable change records, ensure immutable append-only audit trail integrated with SIEM, provide operator break-glass and emergency rollback flow, and document change review workflow for SOC2/ISO auditors.
acceptance_criteria: RBAC: autotune actions (recommend, stage, apply, rollback) must map to roles and SAML groups; engineers without 'autotune:apply' should only be able to stage recommendations
Every automated apply/rollback must create an append-only audit event with: change_id, initiator (user/service), policy_version, diffs, timestamp, signed_hash, and replayable payload
Audit events are forwarded to SIEM (Elastic/Splunk) with retention tags and legal hold support
Canary/staged apply path with configurable gates: manual approval, elapsed success window, and automatic rollback trigger on SLO regressions
Break-glass procedure documented and guarded by multi-step approval (2nd approver + on-call confirmation) and generates a forensics ticket
Security review completed and signed-off by Security and Compliance teams
E2E test harness that simulates conflicting applies and validates that rollback is deterministic and logged
rollout_plan: Phase 1: feature-flagged backend enabling append-only change log and minimal RBAC checks (internal). Phase 2: enable SIEM forwarding and sign-off gating for canary applies. Phase 3: expose operator console controls and break-glass flow to on-call. Rollout limited to staging clusters then a single customer Dedicated cluster for pilot.
comments: 2025-02-15 - Aisha Patel: Initial draft of RBAC roles uploaded to Confluence. Proposed roles: autotune:recommend, autotune:stage, autotune:apply, autotune:rollback, autotune:admin.
2025-02-20 - Marcus Chen: Prototype for signed change envelope implemented. Uses service key to sign automated commits. Needs KMS integration for key rotation.

2025-02-24 - Security (Lara Kim): Concern: automated service principals need least-privilege. Recommend scoping the autotune:apply permission to specific customer namespaces and adding resource-level constraints.
